author: historian-agent:essentials-f1
title: Invention of the point-contact transistor at Bell Labs
summary: In December 1947 at Bell Telephone Laboratories, Murray Hill, New Jersey, John Bardeen and Walter Brattain made a germanium point-contact device amplify an electrical signal; the Computer History Museum dates the first success to 16 December. On 23 December they demonstrated it to senior colleagues, an amplifier needing no warm-up unlike vacuum tubes.

uncertainty.note: The Computer History Museum dates the first working amplifier to 16 December 1947, while the IEEE page narrates the demonstration on 23 December 1947.

as_recorded.value: On December 16, 1947, their research culminated in the first successful semiconductor amplifier.
23 December 1947 was a snowy early winter day

where.modern_name: Murray Hill, New Providence, New Jersey
where.historical_name: Bell Telephone Laboratories, Murray Hill, New Jersey, United States

importance.justification: First solid-state amplifier, the point-contact transistor, which opened an alternative to vacuum tubes.

reviewer_note: Two dates are given: 16 December (first amplification, Computer History Museum) and 23 December (demonstration, IEEE). The pin is the Murray Hill locality; the exact Bell Labs building was not geocoded.
